source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Norwalk, CT campus publishes 4 MW of IT capacity, which is half of all the published data center capacity this site has found in Connecticut.

The state has five mapped facilities, but only two publish a megawatt figure, and those two total 8 MW. This campus is the larger of the two. The other three publish nothing, so the real statewide total is unknown and almost certainly higher than 8 MW. The significance of a 4 MW campus here comes less from its size than from how little else in the state discloses a number at all.

For AI specifically, 4 MW is small. Training clusters are measured in tens or hundreds of megawatts, and this facility's published capacity would not carry one at any meaningful scale. The page also lists 168,000 square feet of technical space, but no rack count, so the power density of the hall is not stated. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 4 MW works out to roughly 100 racks. That is an assumption about rack power, not a figure CyrusOne reports, and at 10 kW per rack the same 4 MW would support about 400 racks. The megawatt number is the published fact, and everything about how it is deployed is inference.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which concerns controls over financial reporting rather than the power or cooling redundancy an AI tenant would weigh. No power redundancy topology, no cooling design, and no address or postal code are published. Nothing in the data says whether accelerators are hosted there, and nothing indicates an announced expansion. The suitability score of 49 rests on published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing.
